heading: Linear SAE error may contain missed features; nonlinear error may resist learning feature sets
definition: the linearly predictable part holds features the SAE has not yet learned, while the nonlinear part is qualitatively different and resists further dictionary learning.
summary: One independent preprint supports the measured separation of linearly predictable error from the remaining, nonlinear error under domain-specific training on Gemma 2 9B. It remains unestablished whether linear error contains features the SAE has not learned and whether nonlinear error resists further dictionary learning—learning a set of features for reconstruction.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at 1–10B for operational component separation and persistence under domain change, with independent evidence restricted to Gemma 2 9B. The original's component-norm predictability comparison also includes Gemma 2 2B and Llama 3.1 8B (arXiv:2410.14670#r6). The full feature-identity and dictionary-resistance interpretation remains unestablished. Other scales are untested in this pack.
suggested_status.reason: The original reports component scaling and retraining differences on Gemma (arXiv:2410.14670#r4; arXiv:2410.14670#r5; arXiv:2410.14670#r7). Its pooled component-norm predictability comparison includes Gemma 2 2B, Gemma 2 9B and Llama 3.1 8B (arXiv:2410.14670#r6). An independent preprint reports lower linear predictability with domain-specific training while nonlinear FVU persists on Gemma 2 9B (arXiv:2508.09363#R1; arXiv:2508.09363#R2; arXiv:2508.09363#R5; arXiv:2508.09363#R6). counts: versions.V4.verdicts.supports.studies = 1; versions.V4.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0; versions.V4.studies_by_size contains only 1-10B. versions.V4.studies_by_family lists only Gemma, but the checker's correction establishes Llama coverage for the original's norm-prediction experiment. R2 applies to the measured separation, with the stronger interpretation still open.
suggested_status.open_questions: Directly identify unlearned real-activation features in linear error; independently repeat component retraining across source SAEs, dictionary architectures and capacities; test nonlinear persistence across layers and model families.

source.title: Decomposing The Dark Matter of Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Joshua Engels; L. Smith; Max Tegmark

original_result.setup: The study varied SAE width and trained separate SAEs on linear and nonlinear error in Gemma 2 9B at layer 20 with approximately 60 active features.
original_result.result: Across widths from 16k to 1m, linear error magnitudes decreased while nonlinear error magnitudes stayed mostly constant. After retraining, the fraction of error variance still unexplained was approximately 0.59 for nonlinear error versus 0.54 for linear error; automated scoring rated features learned from linear error about 5 percentage points higher for interpretability than features learned from nonlinear error.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Reallocating SAE capacity lowered the linear error share without shrinking nonlinear reconstruction error.

untested.basis: Both study headers explicitly list this as untested; the original's supporting feature-identification setup is synthetic. untested.basis: The original's retraining comparison uses a single source SAE and yields a modest FVU gap (arXiv:2410.14670#r7). The independent study explicitly does not test larger or extra dictionaries on nonlinear error. counts: versions.V4.coverage_by_operation.training.studies = 1.

The checker confirms no explicit training-stage comparison.

wording_issues.phrase: holds features the SAE has not yet learned
wording_issues.issue: This assigns a feature identity that neither study directly establishes in real activations. The original's header limits identification evidence to a synthetic setup; retraining and domain comparisons provide indirect evidence.

Nonlinear-error norms are less predictable than linear-error norms in a comparison pooled across 329 SAEs: Gemma 2 2B layer 12, Gemma 2 9B layer 20, Gemma Scope SAEs across layers with L0 closest to 60, and all tested Llama Scope SAEs. Component retraining instead uses one Gemma 2 9B layer-20 source SAE. The records also report automated-interpretability differences; the original's verdict corrections describe the retraining and interpretability gaps as modest. These measurements do not identify a distinct semantic kind.

Evidence supports relative difficulty and persistence under tested conditions. Component retraining yields nonlinear FVU approximately 0.59 versus linear FVU approximately 0.54; nonlinear FVU decreases with width outside the middle-layer setting. The independent domain comparison does not directly test further dictionaries on nonlinear error.

method_sensitivity.what: At layer 20 and L0 approximately 60, increasing SAE width reduces linear-error norms while nonlinear-error norms and nonlinear FVU remain approximately constant. The verdict correction states that nonlinear FVU decreases with width in other layers, restricting the plateau to middle layers.

At Gemma-2-9b layer 20, medical-domain versus broad-domain training changes the reported linear error-vector predictability. Nonlinear FVU persists with overlapping reported ranges. Width and sparsity are swept, but the pack does not provide reliable configuration-specific values.
